segs: On Rosh Hashanah the custom is
to eat an apple in honey,
and we say, "May it be Your will
that You renew for us a good and sweet year."
The matter of the renewal of the year
that the Shabbosos and Roshei Chodashim of the year
each have a holiness of their own,
כָּל שַׁבָּת וְכָל חוֹדֶשׁ לְפִי בְּחִינָתוֹ
every Shabbos and every month according to its aspect.
וּבְהַגִּיעַ הַיּוֹם טוֹב שֶׁל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה
And when the Yom Tov of Rosh Hashanah arrives,
קְדוּשַּׁת כָּל הַזְּמַנִּים עַל הַשָּׁנָה הַבָּאָה
the holiness of all the holy times for the coming year,
to bestow anew an awakening of holiness in the soul,
as at the beginning of Creation.
Therefore it is called the Day of Remembrance,
"For You bring a decree of remembrance before You
for all deeds to be recalled."
And as we say in the tefillah and in the Kiddush of the day:
"And Your word, our King, is true and enduring forever";
that is, the word of Hashem
through which all creatures were created
to be renewed each and every year.
that You renew the year for us for good;
that is, that our heart be renewed in all matters
to conduct ourselves in them in the good way,
which is according to the will of Hashem Yisbarach,
following the way of the Torah,
"Say of the tzaddik that he is good."
וְצַדִּיק נִקְרָא מִי שֶׁשּׁוֹמֵר אֶת דְּרָכָיו
And a tzaddik is one who guards his ways
to walk in the good and upright path
before Him, Yisbarach, in the way of the Torah,
even if he does not yet feel within himself
taste and sweetness in his engagement with holiness
so as to be joyful in his avodah,
"Tzaddikim to light, and the upright to joy,"
where at the start of the sowing
אֵינֶנּוּ יוֹדֵעַ עוֹד מַה יִּצְמַח מִזֶּה
one does not yet know what will grow from it.
But "and for the upright of heart, joy":
taste and sweetness in the avodah,
until joy is born from this in his heart.
And this is the intent of "sweet":
it is the feeling of taste and joy in the heart.
And as an allusion to this
we eat an apple in honey,
עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שַׁבָּת פח, א)
in line with what Chazal said (Shabbos 88a)
that Yisrael are likened to an apple:
מַה תַּפּוּחַ זֶה פִּרְיוֹ קוֹדֵם לְעָלָיו
just as with this apple its fruit comes before its leaves,
so too Yisrael put "we will do" before "we will hear."
that one does the aspect of good
while he does not yet feel the taste,
רַק לַעֲשׂוֹת מַה שֶּׁיִּצְטַוֶּה מֵרְצוֹנוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ
only doing what he is commanded by His will, Yisbarach,
to walk in the way of the Torah.
And "we will hear" is the feeling of taste
so that the sweetness is absorbed into his heart
with joy and with good sense and knowledge;
this is the meaning of "we will hear."
And this is the allusion of the apple
which is the aspect of "we will do," as mentioned above,
the aspect of "Say of the tzaddik that he is good."
And honey alludes to the sweetness of hearing
and understanding with good sense and knowledge,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה מַרְגִּישׁ הַשִּׂמְחָה בְּלִבּוֹ
through which he feels the joy in his heart,
in line with what is said (Shoftim 14:18):
And as above: "and for the upright of heart, joy."
And this is "that You renew for us
that You renew for us a good and sweet year."
"A good year" means in words of Torah,
for "good" without qualification refers to words of Torah,
And it is written (Mishlei 6:23): "And Torah is light."
And the first time "good" is mentioned in the Torah
וַיַּרְא אֱלֹהִים אֶת הָאוֹר כִּי טוֹב
"And Elokim saw the light, that it was good";
corresponding to the five Chumashim of the Torah."
עַל הַפָּסוּק (בְּרֵאשִׁית א, ג) יְהִי אוֹר וַיְהִי אוֹר
on the pasuk (Bereishis 1:3) "Let there be light, and there was light":
"'Let there be light' — this is Pesach,
'and there was light' — this is Rosh Hashanah."
That is, on Pesach there was
the beginning of the revelation of the light that is good,
but afterwards it was hidden from them,
"They went three days in the wilderness
and water means words of Torah,
וּבַזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב ס, א)
And in the holy Zohar (Zohar II 60a):
וְכִי מַאן יָהִיב לְהוּ אוֹרַיְיתָא הָכָא
דְּקוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא תּוֹרָה אִיקְרֵי וְכוּלֵּי
that the Holy One, blessed be He, is called Torah ...."
Meaning: the essence of the light
is that it shine into the heart
that there is One Who created the world;
this is the aim of the entire Torah,
and this is "And Torah is light."
וְעַל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה נֶאֱמַר וַיְהִי אוֹר
And of Rosh Hashanah it is said "and there was light,"
for the light already has existence:
the words of Torah are renewed with new faces
שֶׁבְּכָל שַׁבָּת וְשַׁבָּת יֵשׁ קְדוּשָּׁה מְיוּחֶדֶת
for every Shabbos has a holiness of its own
from the words of Torah of the parashah
וּבְכָל שָׁנָה מִתְחַדֵּשׁ כָּל הַדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה
and every year all the words of Torah are renewed
For in the month of Nissan it is the renewal of the moon,
which receives from the light of the sun,
while Tishrei is the light of the sun itself,
which is the aspect of the Written Torah;
and every year it is studied anew
over the cycle of the year.
corresponding to the years of his reign."
That is, according to his error
his intent in the service was for the sake of Heaven,
הָיָה מְחַדֵּשׁ בְּכָל שָׁנָה פָּנִים אֲחֵרִים
he would innovate each year new facets
which is the book of the service of the korbanos,
and he thought he was intending it for Heaven.
And this is what we ask:
"that You renew for us a good year" —
that the renewal of the year be in words of Torah,
which is the light that is good.
"And sweeter than honey and the drippings of the honeycomb";
that is, that they feel taste in words of Torah,
"This is one who reveals the things
that the Ancient of Days concealed;
and what are they? The reasons of the Torah" —
that they feel taste in words of Torah,
that the words of Torah enter
into the depths of the heart.
And it is written (Koheles 11:7): "And the light is sweet";
that is, when one feels the taste in words of Torah
with the understanding of the heart,
that is the seeing of the light,
in line with what is said (Koheles 1:16):
"And my heart has seen much wisdom."
"Honey and milk are under your tongue,"
And this is the custom of eating an apple in honey,
"Like an apple tree among the trees of the forest":
"Why are Yisrael likened to an apple? ...
so too Yisrael put 'we will do' before 'we will hear'";
for at the time of Mattan Torah
Yisrael were likened to an apple.
And although the pasuk "Like an apple tree ..."
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁהִקְשׁוּ בַּתּוֹסָפוֹת (שָׁם, דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל פִּרְיוֹ)
רַק כֵּיוָן שֶׁנִּמְשַׁל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לְתַפּוּחַ
yet since Hashem Yisbarach is likened to an apple,
Yisrael are likened to an apple as well,
in line with what they said (Tanchuma Kedoshim 2):
"Since you have been sanctified to My Name ...,
הֱיוּ קְדוֹשִׁים כְּשֵׁם שֶׁאֲנִי קָדוֹשׁ וְכוּלֵּי
be holy just as I am holy ....
A parable: to what may this be compared?
To a king who betrothed a woman.
He said to her, 'Since you have been betrothed to my name,
I am king and you are queen;
כְּשֵׁם שֶׁהוּא כְּבוֹדִי כָּךְ הוּא כְּבוֹדֵךְ
just as it is my honor, so it is your honor.'"
So once Hashem Yisbarach is likened to an apple,
Yisrael too are likened to an apple.
And it is written (ibid.): "In His shade I delighted and sat,
and His fruit is sweet to my palate";
וְהוּא עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר וּמָתוֹק הָאוֹר
this is in line with "And the light is sweet."
And this is what we ask:
"that You renew for us a good year" —
with the light of Torah, which is called good;
that there be "and the light is sweet" in words of Torah;
וּמִמֵּילָא נִכְלָל בָּזֶה גַּם כָּל הַטּוֹבוֹת
and with this, all good things are included as well.
מַה שֶּׁנּוֹהֲגִין לֶאֱכוֹל תַּפּוּחַ מָתוֹק בִּדְבַשׁ
As for the custom to eat a sweet apple in honey
and to ask "that You renew for us
why did they choose specifically an apple
(אִדְּרָא נָשֹׂא, זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג קלג, ב)
פָּסִיק שַׂעֲרָא וְאִתְחֲזְיָין תְּרֵין תַּפּוּחִין וְכוּלֵּי
"The hair breaks off, and two apples are revealed ...."
וְהוּא עַל פִּי שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה כז, א)
This follows what they said (Bereishis Rabbah 27:1):
"Great is the power of the Neviim,
who liken the form to its Maker";
וְכֵן רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחָאי גַּם כֵּן
and so too Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai
מְתָאֵר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ כִּבְיָכוֹל בְּצוּרַת אָדָם
describes Hashem Yisbarach, as it were, in the form of a man,
that beneath the hairs of the beard
"'Like an apple tree among the trees of the forest ...':
בְּאוֹר פְּנֵי מֶלֶךְ חַיִּים (מִשְׁלֵי טז, טו)
'In the light of the King's face is life' (Mishlei 16:15);
and we have learned: from these apples
life goes forth to the world ...;
כְּתִיב (בַּמִּדְבָּר ו, כה) יָאֵר ה׳ פָּנָיו אֵלֶיךָ וְכוּלֵּי
it is written (Bamidbar 6:25): 'May Hashem shine His face upon you ...' —
And it is written "and be gracious to you": He will grant you favor.
And favor implies even though one is not deserving,
לֹא שֶׁהָיָה כְּדַאי אֶלָּא שֶׁמָּצָא חֵן
"Not that he was worthy, but that he found favor."
וְכֵן מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּנוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם בִּיקֵּשׁ
Likewise Moshe Rabbeinu, alav hashalom, asked
(Shemos 33:16): "For how then will it be known
that I have found favor in Your eyes ...";
for he did not want to make it depend on his deeds,
to be granted an unearned gift
even if he is not worthy.
כֹּה אָמַר ה׳ מָצָא חֵן בַּמִּדְבָּר וְגוֹמֵר
"Thus says Hashem: They found favor in the wilderness ...";
שֶׁאַף שֶׁהָיָה קִטְרוּג עַל הַדּוֹר הַהוּא
for although there was an accusation against that generation
at the Exodus from Egypt and at the splitting of the Sea —
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (שְׁמוֹת רַבָּה כא, ז וְעוֹד)
as they said (Shemos Rabbah 21:7 and elsewhere) —
nevertheless the generation of the wilderness found
as stated in the holy Zohar
(זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג צב, א וּשְׁאָר מְקוֹמוֹת)
therefore on Rosh Hashanah we eat an apple
to arouse above the light of the King's face
from those two apples, as mentioned above;
and through the shining of the face
there will be "and be gracious to you,"
that we merit an unearned gift
For if it were by way of judgment,
מִי יוּכַל לוֹמַר זִכִּיתִי לִבִּי (מִשְׁלֵי כ, ט)
who could say, "I have purified my heart" (Mishlei 20:9)?
And there are accusations against this;
can we ask for an unearned gift.
וַיְהִי אוֹר דָּא רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה וְכוּלֵּי
"'And there was light' — this is Rosh Hashanah ..." —
on Rosh Hashanah there already is
existence and permanence to the shining of the King's face;
then is the time to ask for the light,
that He shine His face upon us,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה נִזְכֶּה לִמְצִיאַת חֵן
and through this we will merit finding favor.
אָנוּ אֵין לָנוּ אֶלָּא הֶאָרַת פָּנֶיךָ
"We have nothing but the shining of Your face;
save me and we shall be saved";
for through the shining of the face
נִזְכֶּה לִישׁוּעָה עַל יְדֵי מַתְּנַת חִנָּם
we will merit salvation as an unearned gift.
"Fortunate is the people that knows the teruah;
Hashem, in the light of Your face they will walk";
שֶׁבְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה עַל יְדֵי הַתְּקִיעוֹת שׁוֹפָר
for on Rosh Hashanah, through the shofar blasts,
we also merit the shining of the face.
to arouse the light of the King's face,
and we ask "that You renew for us a good year" —
meaning the light that is good
for the first "good" in the Torah
נֶאֱמַר וַיַּרְא אֱלֹהִים אֶת הָאוֹר כִּי טוֹב
is said in: "And Elokim saw the light, that it was good,"
וְאַחַר כָּךְ נֶאֱמַר בְּכָל מַעֲשֵׂה בְרֵאשִׁית
and afterwards it is said of all the work of Creation,
בְּכָל יוֹם וַיַּרְא אֱלֹהִים כִּי טוֹב
on each day: "And Elokim saw that it was good";
that in all the work of Creation
יֵשׁ בְּחִינַת הָאוֹר שֶׁנִּקְרָא כִּי טוֹב
there is the aspect of the light called "that it was good."
וְרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה שֶׁהוּא הָרֹאשׁ שֶׁל הַשָּׁנָה
And Rosh Hashanah is the head of the year,
regarding why it is called Rosh Chodesh
and not "the first of the month":
that it is the head of the month,
therefore one can merit on Rosh Hashanah
that the whole year be good,
that we merit in it the light that is good.
In the Gemara (Shabbos 88a) there is expounded
"Like an apple tree among the trees of the forest" regarding Yisrael,
who are likened to an apple:
מַה תַּפּוּחַ זֶה פִּרְיוֹ קוֹדֵם לְעָלָיו
"Just as with this apple its fruit comes before its leaves,
so too Yisrael put 'we will do' before 'we will hear.'"
We have already noted a difficulty:
"Its clusters — these are the talmidei chachamim;
עָלִין שֶׁבָּהּ אֵלּוּ עַמֵּי הָאָרֶץ וְכוּלֵּי
its leaves — these are the amei ha'aretz ...;
for were it not for the leaves,
According to this, the men of deeds
and the talmidei chachamim are the fruits;
וְכָאן אָמְרוּ עַל שֶׁהִקְדִּימוּ נַעֲשֶׂה לְנִשְׁמָע
yet here they said, of putting "we will do" before "we will hear,"
that it is like an apple whose fruit comes before its leaves,
making the fruit stand for "we will do."
But the "we will do and we will hear" that they said —
that the doing come before the hearing —
in line with what they said (Sanhedrin 99b):
"as though he had made the words of Torah."
וְהוּא עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁמָּצִינוּ בְּפֶסַח שֵׁנִי
It is like what we find with Pesach Sheni,
שֶׁאָמַר לָהֶם מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּנוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
where Moshe Rabbeinu, alav hashalom, said to them
what Hashem will command concerning you";
and we said that "stand" means in prayer,
that they cried from the depth of their heart,
אַף שֶׁלֹּא הָיוּ רְאוּיִם לְקָרְבַּן פֶּסַח
though they were not fit for the korban Pesach,
with this outcry before Hashem Yisbarach,
"I will hear what Hashem will command concerning you"
and in line with what they said (Sanhedrin 8a):
but the daughters of Tzelafchad merited,
and it was written through them."
And this is why they said "we will do" first:
we will make words of Torah;
הַיְינוּ שֶׁיָּאִיר ה׳ לֵידַע הַדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה
that is, that Hashem will give us light to know the words of Torah
and the deed that we are to do,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁמָּצִינוּ בְּאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
as we find with Avraham Avinu, alav hashalom,
שֶׁקִּייֵּם כָּל הַתּוֹרָה עַד שֶׁלֹּא נִתְּנָה
who kept the entire Torah before it was given
and from where did he learn the Torah?
Rather, Hashem Yisbarach shone light into his heart,
and he knew on his own all the words of Torah,
And this is what they said (ibid. 2:3):
"'Let there be light' — this is Avraham";
for he was the first to merit the light.
And this is why they said that they are likened to an apple,
since they put "we will do" before "we will hear":
we will merit the light of Torah;
and this is "its fruit comes before its leaves":
come before the deed and before hearing in order to do.
וּכְתִיב (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים ב, ג) בְּצִלּוֹ חִמַּדְתִּי וְיָשַׁבְתִּי
And it is written (Shir HaShirim 2:3): "In His shade I delighted and sat,
and His fruit is sweet to my palate";
הַיְינוּ בְּצִלּוֹ שֶׁהוּא אוֹר פְּנֵי מֶלֶךְ חַיִּים
that is, "in His shade," which is the light of the King's face that is life,
"and His fruit is sweet to my palate,"
"And the light is sweet, and it is good ...."
And this is why we say "a good and sweet year":
שֶׁנִּזְכֶּה בְּכָל הַשָּׁנָה לְהָאוֹר כִּי טוֹב
that we merit all year the light that is good;
and "sweet," that we feel taste in words of Torah,
And we find, regarding the four who entered the Pardes
"Ben Zoma ... of him the verse says
(מִשְׁלֵי כה, טז) דְּבַשׁ מָצָאתָ אֱכוֹל דַּיֶּיךָּ
(Mishlei 25:16): 'Have you found honey? Eat what suffices you,
lest you be sated with it and vomit it'";
for at times one can receive
more than is fitting for him in the secrets of the Torah,
"'Honey and milk are under your tongue' —
And about this they said "and sweet":
שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ יָאִיר לָנוּ בְּהֶאָרַת פָּנִים
that Hashem Yisbarach shine upon us with the shining of His face
לְקַבֵּל רַק דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה הָרְאוּיִם לָנוּ
to receive only words of Torah fitting for us,
that there be "and the light is sweet,"
that the words of Torah shine in the heart,
And the essence of words of Torah is the light,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁמָּצִינוּ (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה א, ב, ד)
when Yisrael heard "I am Hashem your God,"
"the learning of Torah was implanted in their heart ...."
אַף שֶׁלֹּא שָׁמְעוּ רַק מַאֲמַר אָנֹכִי ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ
Although they heard only the utterance "I am Hashem your God,"
once it shone in their heart in truth
שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הוּא בַּעַל הַכּוֹחוֹת שֶׁלָּהֶם
that Hashem Yisbarach is the Master of their powers —
this is the light of the King's face;
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה זָכוּ לְכָל הַדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה
and through this they merited all the words of Torah,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁזָּכָה אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
just as Avraham Avinu, alav hashalom, merited
and understood with his own mind
לְקַיֵּים כָּל הַדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה עַד שֶׁלֹּא נִתְּנָה
to keep all the words of Torah before it was given.
And to this the apple points,
whose fruit comes before its leaves:
that there be a "making" of words of Torah.
So too we find that it is written (Nechemiah 8:10):
"Eat rich foods and drink sweet drinks ...,
for the day is holy to our Lord."
וְהוּא דְּיוֹם רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה נִקְרָא בַּתִּיקּוּנִים
This is because the day of Rosh Hashanah is called in the Tikkunim
there remains the resh — Rosh Hashanah";
וְהוּא דְּחַג הַזֶּה הוּא נֶגֶד יִצְחָק
That is, this festival corresponds to Yitzchak
and of him we find that he said to Esav
that there was holiness in Esav,
אֲבָל עִיקַּר הַמַּטְעַמִּים הָיוּ עֲבוּר יַעֲקֹב
but the delicacies were really for Yaakov,
דְּאִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג ק, א)
as stated in the holy Zohar (Zohar III 100a):
And this is what is said (Tehillim 89:16):
"Fortunate is the people that knows the teruah,"
and it is stated in the Midrash (Vayikra Rabbah 29:4):
וְכִי אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם אֵין יוֹדְעִין לְהָרִיעַ
"Do the nations of the world not know how to sound the teruah?
how to win over their Creator with the teruah."
And on this the verse concludes:
"Hashem, in the light of Your face they will walk";
שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה זוֹכִין לְהָאוֹר פְּנֵי מֶלֶךְ
for through this they merit the light of the King's face,
"For the day is holy to our Lord":
שֶׁאֵין אוֹכְלִים רַק לִכְבוֹד קְדוּשַּׁת הַיּוֹם
we eat only in honor of the holiness of the day;
and this is "and drink sweet drinks":
that it be as it says, "And the light is sweet,"
that we feel a taste of sweetness in words of Torah
and receive the light in measure, as is fitting,
that it be "eat what suffices you," as mentioned above.
For this reason we eat a sweet apple in honey:
that through the arousal from below
the light of the King's face that is life,
so that the whole year be
a good and sweet year, as stated.
The custom is to eat the head of a sheep
and to ask that we be a head and not a tail
(רְאֵה שֻׁלְחָן עָרוּךְ אוֹרַח חַיִּים תקפג, ב)
We have already said (and it was explained in Parashas Ki Savo)
that the seventh blessing in the parashah there
"Hashem will make you a head and not a tail,"
for this is the completion of the blessings:
when one is refined in all seven middos,
that one is a head to foxes
and nevertheless he is a tail to lions,
regarding the rows before the Sanhedrin:
"Until now I sat at the head;
now you seat me at the tail ...,
that we be a head and not a tail;
הַיְינוּ שֶׁיִּהְיוּ כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל בִּבְחִינַת רָאשִׁים
that is, that all Yisrael be in the aspect of "heads,"
that each one, in his level and his aspect,
and not merely a head to foxes;
rather a head and not a tail,
so that each one of Yisrael be shown
to be, in his level, the choicest and the head.
And this is what is said (ibid.):
וְהָיִיתָ רַק לְמַעְלָה וְלֹא תִהְיֶה לְמַטָּה
"And you shall be only above, and you shall not be below" —
that it no longer be conceivable
that one be, chas v'shalom, below.
This is as they said (Tanchuma Nitzavim 2):
אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁמִּנִּיתִי לָכֶם רָאשִׁים וְכוּלֵּי
you are all equal before Me."
That is, each one of Yisrael
has a portion in the Torah,
a letter or part of a letter,
וְאִם יֶחְסַר אוֹת אוֹ חֵלֶק מֵהָאוֹת
and if a letter or part of a letter is missing
And this is why He said, "You are all equal before Me,"
as it will be in the future,
when there will be no distinction of levels,
"In the future the Holy One, blessed be He,
will make a circle dance for the tzaddikim ...";
and in a circle there is no distinction of levels
And in the Tikkunim (Introduction 1b, and elsewhere),
where he lists the levels of Yisrael
a different name for each attribute,
he counted "heads" corresponding to Kesser Elyon;
corresponds to the attribute of Kesser Elyon,
since Hashem Yisbarach is the head of Yisrael,
And this is what we say: "a head and not a tail."
The custom is to take the head of a sheep
in remembrance of the ram of Yitzchak.
that with Yitzchak we find that he said
וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר עַל יוֹם רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה
and accordingly it is said of the day of Rosh Hashanah
for the day is holy to our Lord";
for when the eating is for the sake of Heaven,
only for the holiness of the day,
and to feel taste in words of Torah,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (קֹהֶלֶת יא, ז) וּמָתוֹק הָאוֹר
as it says (Koheles 11:7): "And the light is sweet."
And the primordial light that was hidden away
is what shines into Chochmah and Binah
from the aspect of Kesser Elyon,
through the upper tip of the yud,
and this is the aspect of "head."
And the entire essential aim of the blasts
הוּא שֶׁיּוֹדְעִים לְפַתּוֹת אֶת בּוֹרְאָן בִּתְרוּעָה
is that they know how to win over their Creator with the teruah,
as stated in the holy Zohar
(הַנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל, זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג צט, ב)
to break the force and strength
And this is what is said (Tehillim 89:16):
"Fortunate is the people that knows the teruah;
Hashem, in the light of Your face they will walk";
שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה זוֹכִין לְהֶאָרַת פָּנִים
for through this they merit the shining of the face
Therefore we eat the head of a sheep
in remembrance of the ram of Yitzchak,
and ask that we be a head and not a tail:
that each one of Yisrael merit
to be refined in his level and aspect up to the head,
שֶׁהוּא כְּנֶגֶד מִדַּת כֶּתֶר עֶלְיוֹן כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל
which corresponds to the attribute of Kesser Elyon, as mentioned above;
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה יִזְכֶּה לְאוֹר הָרִאשׁוֹן
and through this he will merit the primordial light,
the light that is good, as mentioned above.
